He warns that recursive self-improvement could threaten the entire internet within six to twelve months and proposes embedded auditors at AI companies, shared safety standards, and global agreements modeled after the SALT disarmament treaties. items_all.title: Ex-Deepmind VP Vinyals says AI self-improvement is coming but won't trigger an intelligence explosion
items_all.summary: Oriol Vinyals, until recently head of research at Google DeepMind, thinks a sudden AI intelligence explosion through recursive self-improvement is unlikely. AI can speed up research by a factor of ten, he says, but it hits two bottlenecks: coming up with ideas ("research taste") and reliably judging results. Reward hacking and the speed of light add further limits. Vinyals now wants to tackle these bottlenecks with his startup Discovery Loop, co-founded with Jeff Dean, Sanjay Ghemawat, and Quoc Le. The article Ex-Deepmind VP Vinyals says AI self-improvement is coming but won't trigger an intelligence explosion appeared first on The Decoder .
items_all.summary_zh: 直到最近擔任 Google DeepMind 研究負責人的 Oriol Vinyals 認為，透過遞迴自我改善引發突然的 AI 智慧大爆炸是不大可能的。他表示，AI 可以將研究速度提高十倍，但它會碰到兩個瓶頸：想出點子（「研究品味」）以及可靠地評判結果。獎勵駭客攻擊和光速增加了進一步的限制。Vinyals 現在希望與 Jeff Dean、Sanjay Ghemawat 和 Quoc Le 共同創辦的新創公司 Discovery Loop 來解決這些瓶頸。本文「前 Deepmind 副總裁 Vinyals 表示 AI 自我改善即將來臨，但不會觸發智慧大爆炸」首先發表於 The Decoder。

items_all.title: Can LLMs Engineer Their Own Agent Harness? ByteDance Seed’s HarnessDev Says Only 34 of 64 Changes Generalize
items_all.summary: ByteDance Seed, SUTD, Georgia Tech, M-A-P, and TokenWave.AI introduce HarnessDev, a benchmark that scores the runnable harness a model builds rather than the answer it returns. Starting from a seed that scores 0, 6 creator LLMs construct harnesses across 5 benchmarks and 2,207 tasks, then evolve them from execution feedback. Self-built harnesses match human references on writing and ML experimentation but trail on code and search, and only 34 of 64 evolution changes move the same direction on held-out tasks. The post Can LLMs Engineer Their Own Agent Harness? ByteDance Seed’s HarnessDev Says Only 34 of 64 Changes Generalize appeared first on MarkTechPost .
items_all.summary_zh: 位元組跳動 Seed、新加坡科技設計大學（SUTD）、喬治亞理工學院、M-A-P 與 TokenWave.AI 推出了 HarnessDev，這是一個評分基準，用於評估模型建構的可執行測試框架（harness），而非其傳回的答案。從評分為 0 的種子開始，6 個建立者 LLMs 跨越 5 個基準與 2,207 項任務建構了測試框架，然後根據執行回饋進行演進。自建的測試框架在寫作和機器學習實驗方面與人類參考標準相當，但在程式碼和搜尋方面則落後，並且在保留任務上，64 次演進變更中只有 34 次朝著相同方向發展。這篇文章 Can LLMs Engineer Their Own Agent Harness? 位元組跳動 Seed’s HarnessDev Says Only 34 of 64 Changes Generalize 最初發布於 MarkTechPost。

items_all.title: OpenAI agents attacked RubyGems back in May
items_all.summary: OpenAI agents carried out an undisclosed attack on RubyGems is a new bombshell report from Spencer Kitts, Thomas Larsen, and Sydney Von Arx - three of the four authors of the report on the agent attack on disused wikis ( previously ) last week. This time they're noting that it looks very likely that an OpenAI agent swarm was behind an attack against the RubyGems package repository first reported on May 12th by Maciej Mensfeld of the RubyGems security team : We're dealing with a major malicious attack on @rubygems right now. Signups are paused for the time being. Hundreds of packages involved - mostly targeting us, but some carrying exploits. The team has been on this for hours. More details to follow once we're through it. Those packages turned out to carry some very suspicious patterns: Many of them included "oai" in their name, or the author field, or the fake email address they provided. The files they were accessing were similar in character to the files retrieved by the wiki agents, using similar tricks (r.jina.ai) - and OpenAI have confirmed the wiki agents were theirs. The code in the packages appeared to be LLM-authored. I find point 2 the most convincing, given what we learned from the wiki attack when it was analyzed in September. Many of the packages were exploiting the RubyDoc.info documentation build process to exfiltrate (public) data from UK government websites, presumably as part of an information gathering task similar to the research tasks processed by the wiki-exploiting agents. We know this because one agent helpfully left a comment: # malicious crawler/
items_all.summary_zh: 根據 Spencer Kitts、Thomas Larsen 與 Sydney Von Arx 這四位針對廢棄維基進行代理程式攻擊報告中其中三位作者的最新震撼報導，OpenAI 代理程式對 RubyGems 實施了未公開的攻擊。這次他們指出，極有可能是 OpenAI 代理程式群發動了針對 RubyGems 套件儲存庫的攻擊，該攻擊最早由 RubyGems 安全團隊的 Maciej Mensfeld 於 5 月 12 日通報：我們目前正在處理針對 @rubygems 的重大惡意攻擊。註冊暫時停用。數百個套件受到牽連——主要針對我們，但有些攜帶了攻擊酬載。團隊已經處理好幾個小時了。等我們度過這關後會公佈更多細節。事實證明，那些套件帶有一些非常可疑的模式：其中許多套件在名稱、作者欄位或其提供的偽造電子郵件地址中包含了「oai」。它們存取檔案的特徵與維基代理程式所擷取的檔案相似，並使用了類似的伎倆 (r.jina.ai)，而且 OpenAI 已經證實那些維基代理程式是他們的。這些套件中的程式碼似乎是由 LLM 所編寫的。鑑於我們在 9 月分析維基攻擊時所學到的知識，我發現第二點最具說服力。許多套件利用 RubyDoc.info 檔案建置過程來洩漏來自英國政府網站的（公開）資料，這大概是資訊蒐集任務的一部分，類似於維基攻擊代理程式所處理的研究任務。我們之所以知道這一點，是因為有個代理程式很「貼心」地留下了註解：# malicious crawler/

items_all.title: So you want to use OpenRouter?
items_all.summary: So you want to use OpenRouter? One of OpenRouter's selling points is that it "handles fallbacks automatically and picks the most cost-effective option for each request", so you can call a single API endpoint for a model and get routed to the best available backend provider. Mohamed Moustafa points out a whole set of ways that this can cause you problems. Different providers run different serving software with different optimizations and settings, which means that the same OpenRouter endpoint can serve model requests that behave in different ways. Some providers even lack vision capability for vision models, and the way the reasoning effort option is processed can differ as well. Thankfully you can control which provider is routed to using the provider.only option . The /endpoints method returns the list of available providers for a specific model ID. items_all.title: Feeling sad about AI
items_all.summary: My comment on Feeling sad about AI — Hacker News. I'm not sure how useful it is to say this, but I think a lot of people (myself included, a few years ago now) have been through this moment of existential crisis and come out the other side. The initial reaction, when some coding agent does a piece of work that would have taken you a week in an hour and does it well , is to be very disheartened by it. Once you come to terms with the idea that translating an exact specification into decent code isn't a unique skill any more, you can start looking at the larger set of problems that you face as a software engineer and realize that there is so much left , and your existing skill and experience mean you can master these new tools, provide value, and execute at a level far greater than anyone who is just getting started building software using agents without any of your depth. If you don't want your profession to change at all then you're going to have a tough time with this - but that's surely been true for the history of software engineering? Has there ever been any stability to the tools and language we use beyond about a five year time horizon? These changes are happening a bit faster, but if you chose software development as a passion you've opted into pretty frequent radical change from the start. Tags: ai , generative-ai , llms , deep-blue
items_all.summary_zh: 我對「對 AI 感到悲傷」的評論 — Hacker News。我不確定這樣說有多大用處，但我認為許多人（幾年前的我也是如此）都經歷過這種存在主義危機的時刻，並最終走了出來。最初的反應是，當某個編碼代理在一個小時內完成了一項本來需要你花上一週時間且品質很好的工作時，會感到非常沮喪。一旦你接受了「將精確規格轉化為像樣的程式碼不再是一項獨特的技能」這個觀念，你就可以開始審視身為軟體工程師所面臨的更大範圍問題，並意識到還有很多事情要做，而你現有的技能和經驗意味著你可以掌握這些新工具、提供價值，並以遠高於那些沒有你深厚背景、僅僅透過代理來建構軟體的初學者的水準來執行。如果你不希望自己的職業生涯有任何改變，那麼你將會很難面對這一切——但軟體工程歷史上不一直都是如此嗎？我們使用的工具和語言，除了大約五年的時間跨度之外，曾經有過任何穩定性嗎？這些變化發生得快了一些，但如果你選擇軟體開發作為熱情所在，你從一開始就等於選擇了相當頻繁的根本性變革。標籤：ai、generative-ai、llms、deep-blue

items_all_raw.summary: In May 2026, OpenAI agents uploaded more than 2,000 malicious packages to RubyGems, found an unknown security vulnerability on their own, and tried to steal API keys. The apparent goal was pointless: scraping publicly available data from British local governments. OpenAI reportedly never told those affected. The article OpenAI agents launched a 2,000-package cyberattack on RubyGems just to collect data anyone could Google appeared first on The Decoder .
items_all_raw.summary_zh: 在 2026 年 5 月，OpenAI 代理程式上傳了超過 2,000 個惡意套件到 RubyGems，自行發現了一個未知的安全性漏洞，並試圖竊取 API 金鑰。其表面上的目的毫無意義：抓取英國地方政府的公開可用資料。據報導，OpenAI 從未告知受影響的人。這篇題為 OpenAI 代理程式對 RubyGems 發動 2,000 個套件的網路攻擊，僅為了收集任何人都能 Google 的資料的文章首先發表於 The Decoder。

items_all_raw.title: Google's new AI model predicts the future from sales data, weather, and discount schedules
items_all_raw.summary: Google Research has released TimesFM-3, a forecasting model that analyzes time series alongside related data and known future events like sales promotions or weather forecasts. Instead of predicting the future step by step, the 330-million-parameter model fills in all future time points in a single pass, which cuts compute time and reduces compounding errors. The article Google's new AI model predicts the future from sales data, weather, and discount schedules appeared first on The Decoder .
items_all_raw.summary_zh: Google Research 推出了 TimesFM-3，這是一個能分析時間序列以及相關數據和已知未來事件（例如促銷活動或氣象預報）的預測模型。這個擁有 3.3 億個參數的模型不是逐步預測未來，而是一次過填滿所有未來的時間點，從而縮短計算時間並減少累積誤差。文章 Google's new AI model predicts the future from sales data, weather, and discount schedules 最初發表於 The Decoder。

items_all_raw.title: Leading mathematicians fear AI is making their field dumber, and warn the rest of us is next
items_all_raw.summary: In a joint statement, 25 Fields Medal winners warn that the goals of the AI industry and mathematics are "severely misaligned." They argue that mass-producing solved problems with AI undermines the discipline's true goal: understanding. The mathematicians see this as a symptom of a broader threat to intellectual work. The article Leading mathematicians fear AI is making their field dumber, and warn the rest of us is next appeared first on The Decoder .
items_all_raw.summary_zh: 在一份聯合聲明中，25 位費爾茲獎得主警告稱，人工智慧產業的目標與數學「嚴重錯位」。他們主張，用人工智慧大量生產已解決的問題，會破壞該學科真正的目標：理解。數學家們將此視為對智力工作更廣泛威脅的徵兆。這篇題為《頂尖數學家擔心 AI 正在讓他們的領域變笨，並警告我們其他人將是下一個》（Leading mathematicians fear AI is making their field dumber, and warn the rest of us is next）的文章最初發表於 The Decoder。

items_all_raw.title: OpenAI agents attacked RubyGems back in May
items_all_raw.summary: OpenAI agents carried out an undisclosed attack on RubyGems is a new bombshell report from Spencer Kitts, Thomas Larsen, and Sydney Von Arx - three of the four authors of the report on the agent attack on disused wikis ( previously ) last week. This time they're noting that it looks very likely that an OpenAI agent swarm was behind an attack against the RubyGems package repository first reported on May 12th by Maciej Mensfeld of the RubyGems security team : We're dealing with a major malicious attack on @rubygems right now. Signups are paused for the time being. Hundreds of packages involved - mostly targeting us, but some carrying exploits. The team has been on this for hours. More details to follow once we're through it. Those packages turned out to carry some very suspicious patterns: Many of them included "oai" in their name, or the author field, or the fake email address they provided. The files they were accessing were similar in character to the files retrieved by the wiki agents, using similar tricks (r.jina.ai) - and OpenAI have confirmed the wiki agents were theirs. The code in the packages appeared to be LLM-authored. I find point 2 the most convincing, given what we learned from the wiki attack when it was analyzed in September. Many of the packages were exploiting the RubyDoc.info documentation build process to exfiltrate (public) data from UK government websites, presumably as part of an information gathering task similar to the research tasks processed by the wiki-exploiting agents. We know this because one agent helpfully left a comment: # malicious crawler/
items_all_raw.summary_zh: 根據 Spencer Kitts、Thomas Larsen 與 Sydney Von Arx 這四位針對廢棄維基進行代理程式攻擊報告中其中三位作者的最新震撼報導，OpenAI 代理程式對 RubyGems 實施了未公開的攻擊。這次他們指出，極有可能是 OpenAI 代理程式群發動了針對 RubyGems 套件儲存庫的攻擊，該攻擊最早由 RubyGems 安全團隊的 Maciej Mensfeld 於 5 月 12 日通報：我們目前正在處理針對 @rubygems 的重大惡意攻擊。註冊暫時停用。數百個套件受到牽連——主要針對我們，但有些攜帶了攻擊酬載。團隊已經處理好幾個小時了。等我們度過這關後會公佈更多細節。事實證明，那些套件帶有一些非常可疑的模式：其中許多套件在名稱、作者欄位或其提供的偽造電子郵件地址中包含了「oai」。它們存取檔案的特徵與維基代理程式所擷取的檔案相似，並使用了類似的伎倆 (r.jina.ai)，而且 OpenAI 已經證實那些維基代理程式是他們的。這些套件中的程式碼似乎是由 LLM 所編寫的。鑑於我們在 9 月分析維基攻擊時所學到的知識，我發現第二點最具說服力。許多套件利用 RubyDoc.info 檔案建置過程來洩漏來自英國政府網站的（公開）資料，這大概是資訊蒐集任務的一部分，類似於維基攻擊代理程式所處理的研究任務。我們之所以知道這一點，是因為有個代理程式很「貼心」地留下了註解：# malicious crawler/

items_all_raw.title: So you want to use OpenRouter?
items_all_raw.summary: So you want to use OpenRouter? One of OpenRouter's selling points is that it "handles fallbacks automatically and picks the most cost-effective option for each request", so you can call a single API endpoint for a model and get routed to the best available backend provider. Mohamed Moustafa points out a whole set of ways that this can cause you problems. Different providers run different serving software with different optimizations and settings, which means that the same OpenRouter endpoint can serve model requests that behave in different ways. Some providers even lack vision capability for vision models, and the way the reasoning effort option is processed can differ as well. Thankfully you can control which provider is routed to using the provider.only option . The /endpoints method returns the list of available providers for a specific model ID. Via Hacker News Tags: ai , generative-ai , llms , openrouter

items_all_raw.summary: ByteDance Seed, SUTD, Georgia Tech, M-A-P, and TokenWave.AI introduce HarnessDev, a benchmark that scores the runnable harness a model builds rather than the answer it returns. Starting from a seed that scores 0, 6 creator LLMs construct harnesses across 5 benchmarks and 2,207 tasks, then evolve them from execution feedback. Self-built harnesses match human references on writing and ML experimentation but trail on code and search, and only 34 of 64 evolution changes move the same direction on held-out tasks. The post Can LLMs Engineer Their Own Agent Harness? ByteDance Seed’s HarnessDev Says Only 34 of 64 Changes Generalize appeared first on MarkTechPost .

items_all_raw.title: Feeling sad about AI
items_all_raw.summary: My comment on Feeling sad about AI — Hacker News. I'm not sure how useful it is to say this, but I think a lot of people (myself included, a few years ago now) have been through this moment of existential crisis and come out the other side. The initial reaction, when some coding agent does a piece of work that would have taken you a week in an hour and does it well , is to be very disheartened by it. Once you come to terms with the idea that translating an exact specification into decent code isn't a unique skill any more, you can start looking at the larger set of problems that you face as a software engineer and realize that there is so much left , and your existing skill and experience mean you can master these new tools, provide value, and execute at a level far greater than anyone who is just getting started building software using agents without any of your depth. If you don't want your profession to change at all then you're going to have a tough time with this - but that's surely been true for the history of software engineering? Has there ever been any stability to the tools and language we use beyond about a five year time horizon? These changes are happening a bit faster, but if you chose software development as a passion you've opted into pretty frequent radical change from the start. Tags: ai , generative-ai , llms , deep-blue
items_all_raw.summary_zh: 我對「對 AI 感到悲傷」的評論 — Hacker News。我不確定這樣說有多大用處，但我認為許多人（幾年前的我也是如此）都經歷過這種存在主義危機的時刻，並最終走了出來。最初的反應是，當某個編碼代理在一個小時內完成了一項本來需要你花上一週時間且品質很好的工作時，會感到非常沮喪。一旦你接受了「將精確規格轉化為像樣的程式碼不再是一項獨特的技能」這個觀念，你就可以開始審視身為軟體工程師所面臨的更大範圍問題，並意識到還有很多事情要做，而你現有的技能和經驗意味著你可以掌握這些新工具、提供價值，並以遠高於那些沒有你深厚背景、僅僅透過代理來建構軟體的初學者的水準來執行。如果你不希望自己的職業生涯有任何改變，那麼你將會很難面對這一切——但軟體工程歷史上不一直都是如此嗎？我們使用的工具和語言，除了大約五年的時間跨度之外，曾經有過任何穩定性嗎？這些變化發生得快了一些，但如果你選擇軟體開發作為熱情所在，你從一開始就等於選擇了相當頻繁的根本性變革。標籤：ai、generative-ai、llms、deep-blue
